HRA Analysis: AARDIES A STAR (6) was forced to race without cover last time out outside of Exit Eleven and just simply proved too good there pulling away to score a gutsy win. He draws wide again and may be forced to do some work in the run but should be hard to beat again with the benefit of his two runs back from a spell. BLING YOUR A GAME (3) has the draw advantage over his key rivals in this race and has good gate speed which should allow him to make the most of that draw advantage early. He was able to find the front last time out when scoring a huge win there over stablemate Reserved For Me with an even bigger gap to third in that race. SWEET TIMES (5) impressed last time out at Redcliffe when running into third behind Bettor One and San Luca in the final of the Redcliffe Yearling Sale series. He may be shuffled back again in this race and can be running into it late. AARDIES A MOVER (4) ran well on debut to score after securing the right run 1 out 1 back in the run finishing over the top of Reserved For Me. He is likely to have derived good benefit from his debut outing and should run well again sitting close to the speed in the small field. SELECTIONS: BLING YOUR A GAME (3), AARDIES A STAR (6), SWEET TIMES (5), AARDIES A MOVER (4) SUGGESTED BET: AARDIES A STAR (6) to win.

VELOCIS (2) contested a Group 2 last time out where she appeared to have very well luck beginning moderately from gate 1 before being shuffled back to last there and forced to make a wide run into it late. She appears a trotter with good ability and should win plenty of races in QLD. GLADIATRIX (1) draws well in this race and is a horse with excellent gate speed which should see her able to drive through and lead early in this race from the good draw. She was able to lead on return from a spell and was just beaten by Prince Kenny late. She is likely to be better for the run and should run well. DESIRING DIAMONDS (3) should get a good run behind the speed in this race from a soft draw. She battled on fairly last time out behind smart trotter Fredidrivsamercury finishing third. SERENA LOVE (6) made a break last time out which cost her plenty of ground and saw her well beaten behind Iconic Image. She is a trotter with good ability and can do some work in her races. SELECTIONS: VELOCIS (2), GLADIATRIX (1), DESIRING DIAMONDS (3), SERENA LOVE (6) SUGGESTED BET: VELOCIS (2) to win.

FREDIDRIVSAMERCURY (6) sat without cover last time out and always looked to be in control of the race when travelling easily before levelling up to ICONIC IMAGE (2) in the home straight before pulling nicely clear and winning easily. He may be forced to do some work again in this race but is a trotter with above average ability. PRINCE KENNY (1) was a very impressive last start winner when doing plenty of work and proving too good for Gladiatrix. He draws well in this race but doesn’t appear to have a lot of gate speed which could see him shuffled back a touch early. ICONIC IMAGE (2) has good gate speed and should be able to find the front early in this race before having options from there. He led and ran well last time out but was just no match for FREDIDRIVSAMERCURY (6)who sat outside him and proved too good. DORNISH HILL (4) is a kiwi trotter that is first up in QLD in this race having trialled a number of times. He went well enough in his latest trial to suggest he could be competitive in a race of this nature with the right run. SELECTIONS: FREDIDRIVSAMERCURY (6), PRINCE KENNY (1), ICONIC IMAGE (2), DORNISH HILL (4) SUGGESTED BET: FREDIDRIVSAMERCURY (6) to win.

GOLDEN SUNSET (7) was forced to do plenty of work outside the leader last time out and battled on well there behind Sassy Galleon who was too good with the advantage of a handicap. She starts off a 20m handicap in this race and may need to do the work in the run but should go close again. PINNIE (5) made a mid race move last time out before making a break taking her out of play there. She finds a similar race and if she can bring better manners this time she should be running into it late. HIDE AND SEEK (6) can fly away from the stand start and did so last time out when finding the front before handing over to classy trotter Keayang Stuka. He can look to begin quickly again in this race and should be thereabouts late with a similar run in this race. MAJESTIC LAVROS (2) was running on well late last time out into fourth behind Keayang Stuka. He usually begins well from the stand start and should settle in a prominent position in this race which should see him get every chance to run into the money again late. SELECTIONS: GOLDEN SUNSET (7), PINNIE (5), HIDE AND SEEK (6), MAJESTIC LAVROS (2) SUGGESTED BET: GOLDEN SUNSET (7) to win.

LONGSHOT (9) was forced to do plenty of work last time out at this track when fading late into sixth behind Bettor Be Bohdi. He should find this a bit easier and draws to get a good run through in the early stages. WARRAWEE FLYER (2) looks the potential leader in the race from a good draw. She raced behind the leader at this track and trip five starts ago and was able to prove too good there when rating good time winning. She didn’t have a lot of luck last time out in a race taken out by Lulu Lucifer. GOODOLDBOYSANDBEER (11) has a good record at this track and trip and should run well despite the awkward back row draw. He was shuffled back last time out at Redcliffe and couldn’t get into it in a race taken out by subsequent winner The Luvbug. NUMBER ONE RANGER (10) showed very good gate speed to zip across before taking the trail on My Ultimate Milly and battling on well for third there in good time. He looks set to secure a good run off the speed in this race which could generate a good tempo. SELECTIONS: LONGSHOT (9), WARRAWEE FLYER (2), GOODOLDBOYSANDBEER (11), NUMBER ONE RANGER (10) SUGGESTED BET: NUMBER ONE CHANGER (10) to win.

SASSY GALLEON (3) impressed winning last time out when beginning quickly to lead before taking them all the way beating a strong field including Golden Sunset. She has a handicap advantage again in this race and with a good beginning can look to hold the advantage on key rivals in this race over the potentially even more suitable 2138 journey. KEAYANG STUKA (7) was able to work to the lead last time out and held of the late challenge of Hide And Seek in that race who was able to secure the perfect run behind the leader. He may be forced to do some work this time but could be suited by the step back in distance and finds a race without a lot of depth. ZEALOUS SPUR (6) was shuffled back last time out and ran on late into fourth in a race taken out by Sally Galleon over classy trotter Golden Sunset. He should find this a touch easier and may be better suited over the 2138 where he has won 15 of his races. GET USED TO IT (5) did some work last time out and just faded out of it late in a race taken out by Keayang Stuka. He is likely to be better suited stepping back in distance to a distance he has won 10 of his 11 wins at. SELECTIONS: SASSY GALLEON (3), KEAYANG STUKA (7), ZEALOUS SPUR (6), GET USED TO IT (5) SUGGESTED BET: SASSY GALLEON (3) to win.

JAKOB (3) was forced to race without cover last time out and battled on well there for third behind Shards Eclipse at this track. He is likely to have derived a lot of benefit from that outing and if he can find the front he should be hard to beat. SKIP TO ME LOU (9) was forced to race without cover last time out and was just run down late by A Perfect Dance who had a soft run behind the leader in that race. He may be forced to do the work again but looks well placed and should run well again. SO MANY MOMENTS (10) was able to secure a good run on the pegs last time out and battled on well for third behind Debbie Lincoln. This looks a big step back in grade into this race and she draws to do no work early. BART BENTLEY (8) draws awkwardly inside the back row in this race and will likely need a few things to go his way in the run. He was running on nicely late into fourth last time out behind Dragon in what may have been a slightly stronger race. SELECTIONS: JAKOB (3), SKIP TO ME LOU (9), SO MANY MOMENTS (10), BART BENTLEY (8) SUGGESTED BET: JAKOB (3) to win.

HOLD ONTO YA BLING (2) was excellent last time out when sitting close to the speed over the 2138 stand start at Albion Park and finishing 2.2m from Whos Delight. He draws best of the main chances in this race and can hold a prominent position early. GREATGREAT BOULDER (3) ran well last time out at Redcliffe when running on strongly into third behind Dragon. He should settle closer this time and can be running on late again. AMAMI (9) was well beaten last time out after sitting without cover in a race taken out by Waikaka Magic at this track. He should find this a touch easier and looks set to get a good run through early. ILOVEACALENDERGIRL (8) had a gear malfunction last time out and was pulled out of the race there. She draws well in this race to settle close enough on the pegs and should be thereabouts late. SELECTIONS: HOLD ONTO YA BLING (2), GREATGREAT BOULDER (3), AMAMI (9), ILOVEACALENDERGIRL (8) SUGGESTED BET: HOLD ONTO YA BLING (2) to win.

SHADES OF MIKI (12) looks a clear standout on class in this race and looks very hard to beat despite the outside back row draw. He sat without cover outside of a smart horse in Move It Lou and was just able to prove a touch too good. He looks likely to be left to do the work again. DONNIE MAC (11) secured a good run on the speed last time out and was able to prove too good in the Regional Championships consolation. He draws awkwardly on the back row in this race but does appear to be one of the class runners. ANGUS FINN (8) draws awkwardly inside the back row in this race. He led last time out at Newcastle and just faded late into third behind Radiant Amber in a race the winner rated good time. SWEET DREAMS (2) secured a good run last time out at Redcliffe and was running on late behind The Tiger Army. She looks to find a race where she may be able to work to the lead in the early stages and can run well from there. SELECTIONS: SHADES OF MIKI (12), DONNIE MAC (11), ANGUS FINN (8), SWEET DREAMS (2) SUGGESTED BET: SHADES OF MIKI (12) to win.

LOCHINVAR CAMARO (8) was very impressive in defeat last time out when beaten by Vinke B after leading who has since won impressively in heat of the Peak Of The Creek series. He should get a good run through early and will be hard to hold out late. KICK THE SWITCH (1) should have the gate speed to drive through and lead in the early stages of this race from an ideal draw. He got back in the run last time out at Redcliffe and was running on strongly into second behind Tilly Jayne in a race the winner rated good time. MEGS BOY (5) drops back in grade into this race after taking on The CJ Garrard Memorial last time out which was taken out by one of QLDs best pacers in Final Deadline. He draws wide in this race but could look press forward and race in a prominent position and should run well. MAJOR CRUNCH (3) ran a good race two starts ago when running on well late into third at this track behind Barracuda. He draws well in this race and should settle close enough in the run to play a part in the finish again. SELECTIONS: LOCHINVAR CAMARO (8), KICK THE SWITCH (1), MEGS BOY (5), MAJOR CRUNCH (3) SUGGESTED BET: LOCHINVAR CAMARO (8) to win.

FIRE AND PASSION (7) was able to work across to the lead last time out and was able to score a comfortable enough win there over MOVE IT LOU (4). He draws widest in this race but is a very classy horse and can look to press forward and find a prominent position in this race from the wide draw. HAVTIMETODREAM (3) showed gate speed to lead last time out before fading late and being found to have an issue post race after doing a few things wrong in the run. She has excellent gate speed and should be able to work across to the pegs first before having options from there. At her best she is a quality filly. MOVE IT LOU (4) showed excellent gate speed to lead last time out before taking over on Fire And Passion who took up the lead and led all the way there. He comes into this race third up from a spell and should be nearing peak fitness. FUGITIVE (6) drew poorly last time out at this track on the back row and was running on late into fourth behind Cosmic Flyer. He draws awkwardly in this race towards the outside of the front row and can look to be running on late again in this race. SELECTIONS: FIRE AND PASSION (7), HAVTIMETODREAM (3), MOVE IT LOU (4), FUGITIVE (6) SUGGESTED BET: FIRE AND PASSION (7) to win. BACK YA TRUCK UP (2) will look to reverse the result from his debut last start by making the most of drawing inside MYSTERY MAIL (3) this time around. They both performed well in quick time, putting a gap on their rivals. KOOKY (4) brings a different form line to those two, having been competing against the fillies, but seems to be getting better with each run, including last start when doing all the work mid-race in a fast mile rate and battling on well for second. Tactics will be interesting here, as she does possess sharp gate speed when asked. VINJETTA (1) continues to run handy races and earn nice cheques for her connections and will do similar here in the small field, but will need to improve on previous efforts to be a chance of knocking off the favoured runners. Selections:BACK YA TRUCK UP (2), MYSTERY MAIL (3), KOOKY (4), VINJETTA (1)

CRAYONS TO PERFUME (7) looks a handy 4yo mare still on the rise and looks the one to beat again here, despite drawing the outside front-row gate. It will be interesting to see whether connections push the button from out wide and look to assert her dominance, with some good gate speed drawn inside her. SWIATEK LEIS (6) is second-up from a long break and was dominant in winning all three Sires features throughout her juvenile years. It's hard to gauge where she's currently at, but if anywhere near her best, she looks the obvious danger. IM BUTTER BLUE (5) is an interesting runner who has been racing around the Riverina and possesses good gate speed when asked, while GOT THE GLOW (1) will no doubt be looking to kick through early and hold a forward position if she's on her best behaviour. She has put together two strong wins of late, albeit rising in class here. MOVESLIKEALADY (8) will be reliant on the tempo but will no doubt be flashing home late, as she normally does. The remaining runners have been consistent of late but rise in class here, and it's hard to see them finishing on the podium. Selections:CRAYONS TO PERFUME (7), SWIATEK LEIS (6), GOT THE GLOW (1), IM BUTTER BLUE (8)

BARNABY (1) resumes here off a handy trial and looks extremely hard to beat from the pole draw. Expect him to go around in red figures here, despite being first-up from a break. ATOMIC BLACK (5) and IDEN LADY LINCOLN (6) have both been in great form of late and are normally driven on speed, so may look to employ similar tactics again here from their wider front-row draws. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (2) again gets the nice gate to be earning a cheque for his connections, as he usually does, while you would suspect the remaining runners will be battling it out for the minor cheques. Selections:BARNABY (1), ATOMIC BLACK (5), IDEN LADY LINCOLN (6), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (2)

The first of the Youngbloods heats for the junior drivers, where the two-year-old filly in ANN PENNY (4) will again be taking on the older horses but looks to have enough ability to do so. Expect to see some good gate speed from those drawn inside her, including DENVER MAN (2) and GEMMY LOU (3), who are both capable of running a strong race on their day. JUST LIKA DREAM (5) will no doubt be another who attempts to find a forward position and always runs an honest race. CHEYS ANGEL (6) and OUR DANCE MONKEY (7) will be relying on some good tempo up front to allow them to run home strongly from their wide front-row gates, but both possess plenty of ability. HIGH FROSTY (1) could run a cheeky race from the pole draw if he doesn't gain a start in the Sires Final. Although he steps up in grade here, he can't be dismissed. Selections:ANN PENNY (4), DENVER MAN (2), OUR DANCE MONKEY (7), JUST LIKA DREAM (5)

ALWAYS BETTOR (4) will be looking to take advantage of the barrier draw over the other obvious main fancy in LIKEYOUFORAREASON (10). Both ran exceptional last halves in their heat two weeks ago and clearly look the yardsticks for the final here. The only query would be if IYLAC CHAMBER (2) was able to kick up early from the pole draw, should the emergency not gain a start, and decided to hold out ALWAYS BETTOR (4). It wouldn't surprise to see that happen off the strength of IYLAC CHAMBER (2) strong heat win when doing all the work in fast time and still proving too strong. Although the back-row draw hurts LIKEYOUFORAREASON (10), he clearly has plenty of ability, and his third placing in the Derby in August, when making a sustained wide run from the back of the field, showed he's capable of doing work from off the speed. PORT RUN MACHINE (8) could be the one at odds from the inside back-row draw off a hot tempo and clearly has plenty of ability when right. QUARTEIRA (6) possesses plenty of X-factor but draws an awkward gate here, which will make it tough for him, although he could be running home into the exotics. You would expect the remaining runners would need to improve to finish on the podium in what looks a classy Sires Final. Selections:ALWAYS BETTOR (4), LIKEYOUFORAREASON (10), IYLAC CHAMBER (2), PORT RUN MACHINE (8)

A ROCKIN NIGHTMARE (3) will look to take advantage of another handy front-row draw after being checked and subsequently breaking last start. Expect she may look to find the pegs ahead of the polemarker in KING BART (1), who does possess some gate speed when asked, before relinquishing the front to KENYA (5), who should ensure this race is run at an even tempo. He has been racing well but has found one too good on numerous occasions of late. CONSORT (6) draws wide on the front row and will look to slot in somewhere early, and with a nice run in transit, should be running home strongly. TWILIGHT BEACH (2) broke through for a deserving victory last start at big odds but rises slightly in grade again here, while the back-row runners will be relying on some good tempo throughout to allow them to run home strongly in what is one of many even fields on the card. Selections:A ROCKIN NIGHTMARE (3), KENYA (5), CONSORT (6), TWILIGHT BEACH (2)

The Group 3 Golden Apple Final over the 2,200-metre stand, where the two standouts in JACKS ULTIMATE FURY (10) and HORATIUS SPECULO (12) will look to do battle as they did in the heat and clearly look the class horses of the field, despite their backmark handicaps. JACKS ULTIMATE FURY (10) will again look to take advantage of starting off the 20-metre mark and stay ahead of his main danger early, attempting to employ similar tactics to when finding the front in the heat. However, I do expect the front-row horses may not hand up so easily this week, with standing-start veteran ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (5) likely to ensure they're running even quarters from the get-go, which may make it a tad tougher for those backmarkers this week. WAVES OF CHANCE (9) could be the one at odds off the 10-metre mark and clearly possesses plenty of ability when he switches on, whilst PADDO PLUGGER (1) could run a cheeky race from the pole, stripping fitter from his first-up run and being a normally handy beginner from the tapes. Selections:JACKS ULTIMATE FURY (10), HORATIUS SPECULO (12), WAVES OF CHANCE (9), ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (5)

The three-year-old Tasmanian fillies do battle in the Bandbox Final, and as expected following the prelude, it wouldn't surprise to see any runner bob up and take this out. TWILIGHT STORM (7) again draws wide on the front row, as she did in the prelude. However, expect she may have enough speed to find the pegs here, with STAYZBETTER (8) drawing the back row after galloping out last start. She cleared those inside her with some ease last time and would take plenty of running down if able to find the pegs. QUEEN ANASTASIA (4) was hard to miss when galloping on the final corner for no apparent reason before flashing home late to be narrowly beaten. If she puts her best foot forward here, she clearly looks one of the main dangers. MARIANA (3) was scratched from the prelude, so we are still none the wiser as to where her form sits amongst this field, but expect her to be in the finish if right. JILLSTIGER (2) enjoyed the even tempo when winning the prelude, and if able to replicate that performance from her nice draw here, she's another who clearly has the ability to take this out. QUETZALLI (1) will look to take advantage of the pole draw, while ASTORMZABREWEN (6) and STAYZBETTER (8) draw awkward gates and will need the right runs in transit to be finishing strongly. WILLOW STORM (9) was a strong maiden winner last start after only having fair form previously, and it wouldn't surprise to see her blouse them at big odds with further improvement. Selections:TWILIGHT STORM (7), QUEEN ANASTASIA (4), JILLSTIGER (2), MARIANA (3)

The lowest-class event of the night over the short distance, where COLORADO GIRL (2) should be first to the pegs before I suspect she may hand up to stablemate TUFFTIGER (3), who has been driven aggressively in all his starts for the stable thus far. BARBETTE (5) and FEELINKINDALUCKY (7) also possess good gate speed but may be driven more conservatively here from their wide gates, while JAY MILLER (6) will again look to sit on speed and try to out-tough them. Expect a strong tempo throughout, which should suit the back-row runners, where COOLANDCOLLECT (8) could be the one at odds from his soft trailing draw if gaps appear late, while DANCINWIVJOLENE (1) should again earn a cheque for connections from the pole draw. Selections:TUFFTIGER (3), JAY MILLER (6), COLORADO GIRL (2), COOLANDCOLLECT (8)

The final event of the night, which will also conclude the Youngbloods Series, looks very even on paper. There looks to be plenty of gate speed over the mile, with COUNTY COURT JUDGE (1) and INTO THE HARKNESS (2) looking to kick through hard early in an attempt to find a position on speed, while MISS COLLANN (5) possesses dazzling gate speed and may be better suited back to the mile this week. MUZZAME MATE (4) continues to run strong races and will again look to find a position on speed from his middle front-row draw and be hard to hold out late. MIKIYOURSOFINE (6) and MY WAY (7) are consistent pacers but expect they may have to be driven more conservatively here from their wide front-row draws. MR BONDI (10) and MONTGOMERY BURNS (11) appreciate the mile trip and will be relying on a good tempo throughout to allow them to run home strongly, while CALLING BUDDY (8) is an intriguing runner from Queensland. The market may be the best guide with him, but it wouldn't surprise to see him bob up if luck comes his way from the inside back-row draw. Selections:MUZZAME MATE (4), MR BONDI (10), COUNTY COURT JUDGE (1), MIKIYOURSOFINE (6) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: FROSTY DROP (1) looks the likely leader here, and although he can get weary in the concluding stages, he does drop back into a very suitable race from the good draw. He has led and been beaten his last four, but they have been in slightly stronger ratings races than this and the 1720m trip should suit. BEAU BECA (2) was a powerful winner after a lovely trip last Friday at Melton and all his recent form is sound, JUSTLIKEDAVE (8) draws to trail the likely leader and heads here after a good front-running win at Kilmore in October, while ROSBERG (11), SPEEDY HEALY (6) and ROBLEN RANGER (3) are also last-start victors who could threaten with the right trip. Emergency FLIGHT LOUTENANT (10) was an incredible winner after galloping and losing stacks of ground at Geelong recently, and is a huge chance if he gains a start. SELECTIONS: FROSTY DROP (1), BEAU BECA (2), JUSTLIKEDAVE (8), SPEEDY HEALY (6)

OVERVIEW: Fiercely competitive NR up to 42 event where the map and race shape is crucial, and I fancy last-start winner ROCKNROLL RAMBO (1) might dig up and hold the front in an attempt for a second-straight victory from the top. Last Friday, he led from gate four and beat four rivals that reoppose over 1720m. If that eventuates, GOZO MAJOR (8) would get a great chance if able to hold his back. His last two starts have been solid efforts at Melton and Cranbourne, and he might get the run of the race. That said, I’ll side with WOODLEA DIEGO (9), who drops nicely in grade after competitive performances at Kilmore (second) and Melton (fifth) in decent time. TASTE IT (11) made an early break in that race behind ROCKNROLL RAMBO (1) and can bounce back on her recent form, while MY ULTIMATE RUDI (7) is third-up for Tori Hutchins and brings two runner-up placings from Mildura to town. Plenty more can win – including the emergency OUR TRUE COLOURS (10) – so the chances don’t end there. SELECTIONS: WOODLEA DIEGO (9), GOZO MAJOR (8), TASTE IT (11), MY ULTIMATE RUDI (7)

OVERVIEW: CHRISTMAS BABE (2) looks set to take up her usual spot in front and from there HEART OF GRACELAND (1) should get every chance to run her down late. He only beat one rival home at Ballarat last week, but did hit the line well when clear to only be beaten 7.5m, and also ran okay in two races of higher grade than this before that. Certainly wouldn’t be taking short odds, but he looks set to fight out the finish. MONEY TALKS (10) was a mile back but made up ground in the race won by $101 outsider MODERN HOPE (11) on November 16 at Maryborough and looms as a key chance, fast beginner CHRISTMAS BABE (2) rarely wins but will give herself every opportunity to finish in the placings from the front over 1720m as she has her last two, while Jonathan O’Connor stablemates BROWN EYED KATE (4) and ITGETSBETTER (6) are both running well of late and can certainly win with luck. SELECTIONS: HEART OF GRACELAND (1), MONEY TALKS (10), CHRISTMAS BABE (2), BROWN EYED KATE (4)

OVERVIEW: MIGHTY JOLT (8) was well held in a hot race behind Golden Tribe on Saturday night, but the drop back in grade and to the soft inside back row draw behind the potential early leader in SHAZZA LOVE (1) gives him a great chance of success. Two runs back, he led, handed to My Little Bo and cut the margin to a head in what was a good effort. Happy his way. INVITATION ONLY (4) ran a ripper first-up from a break at Melton last Friday when he worked a touch early, went back to last and sprinted home for sixth – beaten 7.3m – behind Happily. LAMBRO MACH (5) was well fancied on Saturday night, looked the winner at the corner and wasn’t beaten far into fourth behind Sols Me Name, while CRIME WRITER (7) has an awkward draw but is dropping back from the Horsham Pacing Cup where he had no luck after locking wheels early. SELECTIONS: MIGHTY JOLT (8), INVITATION ONLY (4), LAMBRO MACH (5), CRIME WRITER (7)

OVERVIEW: CYCLONE JENNI (6) was a little plain from the tail of the field at Cranbourne on November 15, but you can be forgiven when coming from back and wide at that track. She was outclassed in a heat of the Victoria Oaks before that, but the prior form is very good, including a win and an unlucky third in the Vicbred Silver final at Melton behind Alot Like Jeannie. She’s fast at her best and I’m hoping she can storm over the top. RAKAROMPA (1) draws to settle in behind likely early leader SPUN SILVER (2) and would be a threat from there, BLACKINDEED (5) beat RAKAROMPA (1) home when they clashed at Kilmore last time out and has been very consistent of late, while HARLEY LANE (8) produced a much better effort than CYCLONE JENNI (6) in that race at Cranbourne recently and can certainly win if she gets the right trip from inside the back row. YNOBE NOVA (3) was a huge Mount Gambier winner last time out and beat subsequent victor Spook Crocker in the process, while MATRIARCH DAISY (4) was a good runner-up placegetter at Cranbourne latest and is another winning hope. SELECTIONS: CYCLONE JENNI (6), RAKAROMPA (1), BLACKINDEED (5), HARLEY LANE (8)

OVERVIEW: Andy Gath’s new stable recruit WHIRLY MAURZ (9) has won her past three starts as a short-priced favourite and again looks the horse to beat despite creeping up in grade. She’s in good form, and while she might go around a little under the odds, it’s hard to tip against her. That said, I’m confident MIDNIGHT MOJO (5) will run a good race and I’m happy to back her on the each-way if the price allows. She hasn’t been beaten far and has run home well in recent starts, which have been marginally higher grade events than this. LINE UP JACQUIE (3) showed great gate speed to lead and looked the winner up the straight at Cranbourne first-up before just fading late, while MISS PIGGY WIGGY (7) keeps running placings at good odds and can certainly fill the top four despite the wide alley. BACK: MIDNIGHT MOJO (5) – 2 units (each-way) SELECTIONS: WHIRLY MAURZ (9), MIDNIGHT MOJO (5), LINE UP JACQUI (3), MISS PIGGY WIGGY (7)

OVERVIEW: Been thinking HANDLER (5) has been ready to win a race for some time now, and this shapes as a lovely chance in an even-looking 0-60 grade event. Rob O’Connell’s five-year-old has only had the 17 career starts and appears to have his fair share of ability. Last time out, he was completely outclassed but did a good job to slide into fourth behind top-liner Cardigan Dan in a 54.58 last half of his own. The effort prior was also good when he closed nicely for third behind Popcornfriday in a higher-class race than this. Happy his way. OUR SWEET JEANNIE (8) is the sole runner on the back row and heads here following a good win from back in the field at Shepparton and an earlier effort at Charlton back in mid-September when she broke, was a mile off them at the bell and chased hard to only be beaten 13.3m. She’s a handy mare and a key chance. OOH AH LISTAH (2) claimed a deserved victory – beating subsequent winner Buildthemanastatue – at Melton and ran okay for fourth at big odds last weekend, while BREATHE EASY (1) draws well, has the gate speed to lead and finished third in the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup Final last Friday, just ahead of COOL STORY (7), who is another that can win despite an awkward gate. BACK: HANDLER (5) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: HANDLER (5), OUR SWEET JEANNIE (8), OOH AH LISTAH (2), BREATH EASY (1)

OVERVIEW: Plenty of chances in this event for the trotters where WIND STORM (5) brings in some exciting form from early in her campaign. She’s won both starts this preparation in good style, with the first being a dominant front-running success at Maryborough and then a tough death seat triumph at Melton on November 11 when she was the sole runner in the running line for much of the race. She’s been winning against easier opposition than this, but there’s good scope there as she heads here at start 12. AGAINST THE BRIDLE (7) ran well for second in a stronger race at Ballarat last week and bolted in by 8.5m at Melton back on October 9, BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (3) is flying with three wins and a narrow second this campaign, while SETTLE THE BILL (1) and MYHEARTBEATSTRUE (4) are other winning contenders. SELECTIONS: WIND STORM (5), AGAINST THE BRIDLE (7), BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (3), SETTLE THE BILL (1)

OVERVIEW: ALWAYS BE VICKI (1) looked a tragedy beaten on debut at Kilmore when she led, made a gait break approaching the home turn, recovered and flashed late to just miss the well-fancied Catch A Butterfly. She draws well here and looks the one to be with in this two-year-old contest. SOCIAL OUTING (6) is first-up from Queensland where he won his last start at Redcliffe and presents here following two trial victories at Melton for new trainer Drew Georgeallis, STERLING GIGI (5) is a one-time winner and has been competitive his past few, IDEAL HIGH (3) chased home a smart pair in Mister Threeofive and I Am Molly – a subsequent winner – last start at Cranbourne and is one to consider from the astute stable of Matthew Craven, as is DIAMOND AURORA (2) who started favourite on debut at Melton on October 21 and ran home okay for second despite being well beaten by Gatsby. BACK: ALWAYS BE VICKI (1) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: ALWAYS BE VICKI (1), SOCIAL OUTING (6), STERLING GIGI (5), IDEAL HIGH (3) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R6 #5 MIDNIGHT MOJO – 2 units (each-way) R7 #5 HANDLER – 3 units (win) R9 #1 ALWAYS BE VICKI – 3 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 1,2,6,8,10/7,8,9,10,11/1,2,4,6,10/4,5,8 QUADDIE 1,5,6,8/5,9/1,2,5,8/3,5,7 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:STEEL THE MOMENT (13) was able to win a stronger race than this last week, sitting near last off a good early tempo and steaming home to win in very quick time for this grade. He's likely to map similarly, but the front row doesn't appear to boast the same strength, and with the right trail, he's in the type of form to unleash another powerful finish. Herbertson returns and has driven seven of his eight career victories. WHERE IS WOODY (4) presents as one of the most in-form runners at city-class level and gets a good draw from which he can show his versatility. Last time out, he was excellent when bumping into a hot field, showing early speed to take cover before coming again late. He's been doing very well for the new stable, and a win is close. KING SAINT (9) gets the trailing draw to have striking options over the final lap. He mapped well last week, but the leader just didn't give him enough momentum, and he should have finished closer. He's going much better than his form reads. TOPSIES BLING (12) came through the same race as the top pick and was only narrowly beaten. She too should get a similar trip and is suited to race well again. There are a few others who have claims but may find this line-up tougher, including MONSIEUR FLAMEL (2), YANKEE RAIN (3) and MY ATLANTIS (5), while KATUNGA EXPRESS (6), EL LAZZAR (7) and SCHERGER THAT (8) are going well but have tricky draws. SELECTIONS:STEEL THE MOMENT (13), WHERE IS WOODY (4), KING SAINT (9), TOPSIES BLING (12)

OVERVIEW:MEADOW VALLEY STAR (12) looks very well suited under mobile conditions, having been conceding some sizeable handicaps to members of this opposition at standing starts recently. He's a horse who's raced at stronger levels throughout his career, and while he's yet to win in seven starts for the new stable, those runs have been in difficult set-ups and stronger company, with many still full of merit. He may represent decent value in what appears to be a drop in class. KEAYANG MINNESOTA (13) has won five in a row coming into this as an OD runner, and on the ratings scale, her latest victory strengthens the case for the top pick. She had a 20-metre head start on Meadow Valley Star last time and beat him by five metres. She's with the gun stable when it comes to trotters and commands respect. CARLA PIXIE (9) won here last week but was afforded a great trip when able to use the front-row draw to map behind the leader. This is a different task, but she has claims again. SAMMY HALLER (5) is a quick beginner and could cross to the pegs here, which is an advantage over the short trip, and now has added fitness. DISTANT SUN (8) has been racing well from better draws but looks the best of the rest despite needing luck. BACK: MEADOW VALLEY STAR (12) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS:MEADOW VALLEY STAR (12), KEAYANG MINNESOTA (13), CARLA PIXIE (9), SAMMY HALLER (5)

OVERVIEW:RIVER STORM (1) is a quality 3yo who has proven himself when dropping out of the elite company of his age group, winning in good time on the past two occasions he's done so. Even though that's been in provincial grade, those races have come up quite strong, so while this presents as more challenging, he looks up to it. He's a lightning-fast beginner, so expect him to get a comfortable lead and take plenty of catching. CAPTAIN MOONLIGHT (11) has quickly proven his quality since moving to Australia for the Jack stable, winning twice here at Melton and displaying excellent ability and versatility in those victories. He's earned the back-row draw on the score of ratings, and the claim of Tasmyn Potter, who drove him to victory last time, is a plus. GUNFORHIRE (10) is racing much better than his form suggests, having been taking on stronger company from bad draws and putting down some good sectionals. He can sweep home well from this draw. EARL OF PEMBROKE (8) gets the likely coveted leader's back position here, which will enable him to race better than his recent numerical form suggests. MONTANA PRIDE (2), SECRET SERVICE AGENT (3) and ZANDA MAN (9) all look next best for the exotics. BACK: RIVER STORM (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:RIVER STORM (1), CAPTAIN MOONLIGHT (11), GUNFORHIRE (10), EARL OF PEMBROKE (8)

OVERVIEW:WINCHESTER BOY (6) has been terrific in his two career starts, beating up on a weaker field on debut before mapping negatively last time in a strong race where they ran time, yet still hitting the line strongly. On that pattern, the map could be sticky again, but the make-up of this race presents an opportunity to press forward over the short trip. The ability is there, and he has a driver who's one of the best tacticians in the business. SPOOKY MOTH (3) is from the leading Emma Stewart stable, which is always the benchmark in age-group racing, and this 2yo filly showed plenty of promise on debut when 2nd behind the smart Twigstar. She showed good gate speed on that occasion and was left with too much to do in a race that developed into a sprint home. She has the barrier draw and map advantage over her key rivals here to break her maiden. BETTORBUST (10) has experience on his side and is developing nicely, performing well from bad draws and putting down some strong sectionals. As an OD runner, the map is a disadvantage but look for him to be doing his best work late. They look to be the key winning hopes, with OZZIE TART (8), LANIKAI WARRIOR (9) and LOUS MAMBO (7) the best chances for the minor money. BACK: WINCHESTER BOY (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:WINCHESTER BOY (6), SPOOKY MOTH (3), BETTORBUST (10), OZZIE TART (8)

OVERVIEW: A high-quality FFA where the map positions after 800m will say plenty about the result. SIR JIMMY (1) may represent some value in this race, as he's going much better than his numerical form reads, having drawn poorly. He was able to lead two runs back in a slightly weaker FFA, but hopefully he can show enough speed to take a trail on the right runner here and get his chance along the sprint lane. From this draw, he's more than capable of getting the job done should the map work out. BULLETPROOF BOY (5) is at an interesting point in his career. Long regarded as one of Victoria's best fast-class horses, he's provided more questions than answers this preparation. He galloped at the start in Sydney last week but earned that trip with a great 3rd the start prior when coming off the back row. He's versatile, and while he may be better over the mile these days, he commands respect. YAMBUKIAN (3) has been good in his three runs back from a break, having to work early in most of those races, which were run in quick overall times. Drawing in close again helps, and he doesn't know how to run a bad race. CATCH A WAVE (6) has been a superstar of the sport, and on occasions this season, he's shown he's still got it, but last week at Menangle was a real head-scratcher after having every hope. If his map works out favourably, he can bounce back. FORTY LOVE (8) could be the one to benefit if the big guns off the front row overcook things early. He's another who's just so tough and rarely runs a bad race, but he's dependent on luck here. SELECTIONS:SIR JIMMY (1), BULLETPROOF BOY (5), YAMBUKIAN (3), CATCH A WAVE (6)

OVERVIEW:OUR VINCENT CAN GO (2) has been racing very well without winning here at Melton, as evidenced last week in a higher-rated race when finishing 4th after mapping negatively and finding the line well. He can afford a more positive drive this week and prove hard to beat with a favourable map. Ewa Justice has had only one drive on him, back in 2023 as a 3yo, when they led all the way. KEAYANG VIPER (4) looked to have every hope here last week, but to be fair, that was slightly harder than what she faces here. She's done it all in one preparation this season, so she's a gutsy mare who commands respect. OLLIES THE BOSS (3) has the gate speed to map favourably and is always an honest type. He's perhaps better over the mile, but don't dismiss him. SCHWARZ (6) does have a tricky draw to overcome but gets Herbertson to negate that. This is a drop in grade. Look for sharp improvement. The chances don't end there, with CLYMENUS (1) sure to get a soft run as a knockout chance, while KOMODO (5) and ROYAL APPOINTMENT (7) and DIAMOND ECLIPSE (8) all have tricky draws to overcome but are hard to bin considering they've been racing well in strong grade. SELECTIONS:OUR VINCENT CAN GO (2), KEAYANG VIPER (4), OLLIES THE BOSS (3), SCHWARZ (6)

OVERVIEW:FRANKS ALOT (5) has shown decent ability in his four career runs, winning his maiden in solid fashion against a moderate line-up three runs back before leading and only narrowly being run down last time. He looks to be improving with each run, can press forward and look for the top here, and appears the best option in a line-up that's hard to trust. SYDTHESLOTH (7) put it all together last time with a big win at Echuca, where he was able to find the lead and was far too good for them. With natural improvement, that progression keeps him in with strong claims here despite the draw. KING OF NORMANDY (6) will no doubt create plenty of interest having his first run for Andy Gath, who's a magician with trotters, but he'll need to cast a spell based on what the horse has shown at the trials and on debut, where he got it all wrong as a very short-priced favourite. If you take the odds, you're backing the trainer more than anything on what's been exposed. This is such a tricky race that I wouldn't talk you out of taking the field in the Quaddie, as so many of these do things wrong. HEAVENLY GLOW (1), NO REPENTANCE (2) and ASONGOFTHEHEART (9) all have claims in a low-confidence race. SELECTIONS:FRANKS ALOT (5), SYDTHESLOTH (7), KING OF NORMANDY (6), ASONGOFTHEHEART (9)

OVERVIEW:IRON WOMEN (7), despite the draw, must be the starting point here. Dropping back in class and largely taking on a field of her own sex, she looks very well graded. She has very good early gate speed, and I wouldn't be surprised to see her find the top here, but even if she doesn't lead, she has the grit to sit parked and prove too strong for these over the short trip. The expert trainer/driver combination also appeals. CLAUDYS HERO (4) was very well backed at his first run for the Ashwood stable but did things wrong, galloping and putting himself out of contention. There may be something behind that market support, so from a favourable draw, he certainly deserves another chance, and his best form is right up to a race like this. CENTURION DREAM (5) is also back in grade and gets the 'Herb Factor' to lift her another gear. The stable is racing well and demands respect. ZARSKI (6) has been racing well for the Bellman stable and was a good winner last time out when able to lead, beating some of these. I DREAM OF MILLIE (2) has early speed and is getting closer, but this is a step up, and she has minor claims. LITTLE MISS MORGAN (8) has ability and will have admirers but has been costly when coming to Melton. BACK: IRON WOMEN (7) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:IRON WOMEN (7), CLAUDYS HERO (4), CENTURION DREAM (5), ZARSKI (6)

OVERVIEW:CRACKERJACK (7) has been excellent since coming from NZ, taking on much better grade than he meets here and missing a place for the first time last start when well up in grade and first up from a break. He let down well there before understandably knocking up late over the longer distance. He's the best horse in the race, and although he's far from the finished product, this race could launch him towards better races in January. MORE WANTED (5) comes back to mobile conditions and a favourable draw and has been racing well without winning this preparation. While he's better over more distance, if he gets the right map, he's a solid hope. MAORIS MAC (3) came through the same race as the top pick and got well back there. Her two runs prior were very good, and she looks to get a favourable map to be within striking distance. KYVALLEY MAVEN (6) is a consistent type who often races well over the shorter trip, and while the map may be a little sticky for him, expect him to be in the finish. TIMMY TURTLE (1) has early speed, but this is a step up, and he has minor claims. FOUROUTOFFIVE (4) has ability and is a tough type, but I just have a few in front of him. BACK: CRACKERJACK (7) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:CRACKERJACK (7), MORE WANTED (5), MAORIS MAC (3), KYVALLEY MAVEN (6)

OVERVIEW: It's Stawell Cup Day, and we kick off a bumper 10-race program with a challenging maiden. KEAYANG HARMONY (1) is a 4yo maiden mare from the astute Marg and Paddy Lee stable. She's had two trials, finding the line quite well behind a reasonably smart one in the first of those. The stable has a habit of producing on race day, and the horses given time to mature often perform well when produced in these maiden and lower-graded affairs. There's a bit of guesswork, but the stable instils confidence. BELLEVUE BOY (5) may be the best on exposed form, showing good speed from the pole on debut and attempting to lead all the way, only to be run down by the odds-on favourite. He'll derive benefit from that outing, and another likely positive drive will see him in it for a long way. WATCH HIM DANCE (2) is now third up from a break and was kept safe in the market last time behind a handy one. He's still lacking a bit of confidence in his action but has the right driver to keep his mind on the job. FRENCH PLEASURE (8) can do a few things wrong, but if she gets away safely, she should get a soft run thereafter. She's had to work hard in her races recently, and an economical trip could see an improvement in form. NOCOMMENT (6) is first up since April and was racing well from better draws at Mildura, but I'd prefer to see her this time given the set-up. SELECTIONS:KEAYANG HARMONY (1), BELLEVUE BOY (5), WATCH HIM DANCE (2), FRENCH PLEASURE (8)

OVERVIEW:COLLEAGUES (3) is an eight-start maiden, but all indications are that a win isn't far away. He has a strong SP profile to suggest the ability is there, but did things wrong in two of his past four runs to let punters down. Last time out, Ellen Tormey decided to let him run, and he led up and gave plenty of cheek, only to be run down by a smart one in the shadows of the post. If he brings his manners, he's the one to catch. SOLO SAPPHIRE (2) looks the big improver with James Herbertson aboard, who is without question the go-to driver of the meeting. He drove her from an unfavourable draw last time out, and she found the line much better. From a more positive set-up, expect her to deliver a stronger performance. BILLYSOPHIA (6) surprised with a much better run last time out, where she was able to lead from an inside draw and go close to winning despite suffering a flat tyre. A repeat performance will see her go close. BAGSHOT OLLIE (1) is first up off a couple of trials and looks to get a soft map with a positive getaway. He was able to place and get closer last preparation, so the draw helps in a race of this nature. SUMMIT MEETING (5) should be fitter second up and hasn't brought her best manners to the track in her three starts. There was slight improvement last time, so she's worth keeping safe. SELECTIONS:COLLEAGUES (3), SOLO SAPPHIRE (2), BILLYSOPHIA (6), BAGSHOT OLLIE (1)

OVERVIEW: A mixed 2yo and 3yo maiden with not a lot of form to get keen on. That's why CHAMPAGNE PROBLEMS (1) stands out despite being a 2yo giving away experience. He was terrific last week at Horsham, where he drew awkwardly on the back row, but the driver had no issues putting him into the race outside the leader. He hit the front, only to be shaded by the odds-on favourite in the closing stages. Drawn better now to show speed from the pole, he can look to lead or sit behind the leader and prove hard to beat. KEAYANG ALABAMA (3) is a 3yo who will be driven hard to head him off at the start and look for the lead but was beaten home by the top pick fair and square last week, so would need a better trip to turn the tables. FLY HIGH MICKEY (6) is a 2yo who's earned market respect in his two career runs on the back of a solid trial, but to be fair, he was a little plain in those efforts. The stable is astute with youngsters, so keep him in calculations as a possible improver. SEABLASTER (8) has a good driver and a soft peg-line draw, so he may be one who can improve with an economical run. HIWAYTHREENINENINE (2) changes stables, and while the form isn't there, it's worth keeping an eye on the market. SELECTIONS:CHAMPAGNE PROBLEMS (1), KEAYANG ALABAMA (3), FLY HIGH MICKEY (6), SEABLASTER (8)

OVERVIEW: A standing start for the trotters, with the front line being the 10-metre mark. NEDZA THRILLER (3) is adept under standing-start conditions and has been consistent this season, particularly in races over the middle distance. With a quick beginning here, he's capable of taking up the running and proving hard to catch. CONNIES PRESIDENT (7) brings the best overall form into a race of this calibre but has an extra 10 metres to make up on the top pick and can be a little unreliable from the tapes. He was good last week when 3rd in a race tougher than this, so can go close again. ATABOY CHARLIE (1) has plenty of form around that pair and didn't have much luck here last week when, after mapping well, he was dragged back before finding the line well when the passing lane became available. He's in the mix. HAPPY ESCAPE (6) has been consistent under these conditions in recent times despite being an OD runner. His positive SP profile will again see him popular with punters, and he deserves consideration. ALABAMA MAY (4) is another who's been racing well enough, but she's having her first try from the stand. If she gets away safely, she can be in the finish, but I'd prefer to watch on this occasion. MATISOFF (10) is also in form but will be giving key rivals a start from the handicap and may need some luck. SELECTIONS:NEDZA THRILLER (3), CONNIES PRESIDENT (7), ATABOY CHARLIE (1), HAPPY ESCAPE (6)

OVERVIEW:BIZZNESS CLASS (8) has been racing up in grade and will appreciate this class, coming out of the heats of the Stawell Cup and effectively treating this as a consolation. He gets in so well on ratings with the claim, and if you go back four and five runs, he was racing at Melton in much stronger grade and placing, a level many of these couldn't reach at this stage. Being the sole runner off the back row, he can position himself well and let down strongly late. EASTBRO KAZ (2) has good early gate speed, and you can expect Bellman to give her a positive drive from the soft marble. She was good in a stronger race two runs back, where she led and handed over, and looks to get the right map now to receive every chance. OCEAN AVENUE (5) has early speed and was solid last week from a softer draw when running 2nd in a stronger race than he faces here. You get a top driver aboard in Jason Lee to press forward and give him every chance. He's the testing material off the front row. GOLD IN PARIS (6) is a mare capable of much more than her current form suggests, having raced up in grade and from unfavourable draws. Some of her best form this preparation has come when Herbertson has partnered her. BACK: BIZZNESS CLASS (8) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:BIZZNESS CLASS (8), EASTBRO KAZ (2), OCEAN AVENUE (5), GOLD IN PARIS (6)

OVERVIEW:HOME AND DRY (8) finds the most suitable race he's been in for some time and at a track he's raced well at in the past. There looks to be a lot of speed and not much strength off the front row, so the better-rated back-row runners appear suited here. Most importantly, you get the country's best driver in James Herbertson, who's adept at this track and striking at a 23%-win rate for the season. THE MOUNTAIN (5) can show speed from this draw and has been much better in his past couple of runs in higher-rated races. Kerryn Manning is the leading driver at this track, which is another plus. WATCH IT HAPPEN (1) will be doing his best to hunt up from the inside and take a forward position here. His placings a few runs back were good when he was able to get a positive map, so look for him to be an improver. ICANMOTOR (3) can map softly from the draw and has minor claims, and Jordan Leedham is a driver in form, while SWISS LIGHTNING (6) might be a sneaky one to keep an eye on. He has early speed and has been racing a bit better than his form suggests; he'll just need some luck. SELECTIONS:HOME AND DRY (8), THE MOUNTAIN (5), WATCH IT HAPPEN (1), SWISS LIGHTNING (6)

OVERVIEW: An intriguing edition of the Stawell Trotters Cup, where several runners progress through last weekend's Horsham feature won by Keayang Minnesota. A horse that was scratched from that event was CRUSHER CLYDE (11), who's been kept fresh for this assignment, where he starts from the 10-metre tapes. He's trialled twice at Terang behind the pacers and brings in strong form from Melton last campaign, which closed with a strong victory on March 7. He's won five from eight, hails from the powerhouse trotting barn of Team Lee and looks to be on an upward spiral. There were plenty of good efforts behind the winner at Horsham, including ARTIGAS (4), who stepped sharply, took cover on fellow fast beginner CHAMPAGNE CHARLEY (6) and ended up three pegs behind the winner. He didn't have much room late and was only beaten 3.4m. If he steps quickly again and finds the pegs, I suspect Aaron Dunn will try different tactics around the tight Stawell circuit. MEADOW VALLEY STAR (12) has the back mark of 20m, as he did at Horsham when closing hard late in limited room, and he's certainly good enough to give this a shake. SCAR (1) produced a massive run in defeat as the rank outsider there, even after being caught in the breeze. A great race with more winning hopes than those mentioned! BACK: CRUSHER CLYDE (11) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:CRUSHER CLYDE (11), ARTIGAS (4), MEADOW VALLEY STAR (12), SCAR (1)

OVERVIEW:MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (10) is one of the best exports out of the Mildura region in some time, and he looks a great chance of landing the Stawell Pacing Cup Final. This $20,000 race is the culmination of a three-heat series, with Andrew Vozlic's charge sitting parked and winning tough in the last of the qualifiers at Horsham on Sunday. It was a really good performance given the trip and followed a front-running success at Mildura. He draws nicely on the back row and will be hard to hold out. LOUGLE (11) won the Maryborough heat on November 16 in similar style. He worked forward and sat parked before charging clear for a decisive victory. That followed a race at Melton where he looked destined to fight out the finish before breaking in the straight. He's a good horse on the way up. It might sound silly that connections were disappointed with gate one for TO THE NINES (1), but his lack of gate speed is a worry. That said, if he can dig up and hold a prominent position on the fence, he'll take plenty of beating following his fourth in the Maryborough heat and third in the Horsham qualifier. The other heat winner was KING KASEY (8), who led and dominated at Ararat before doing the same in another race at Ballarat last week. He's a promising pacer on the rise and can win despite the sticky gate behind a slow starter. While only outside winning hopes, LUVA SCRAP (9), EASTBRO KOZZY (4) and the speedy ALL BLAZING GUNS (7) are among others to consider for the back end of trifectas and first fours. BACK: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (10) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (10), LOUGLE (11), TO THE NINES (1), KING KASEY (8)

OVERVIEW:AMERICAN SQUARED (8) could be the beneficiary of a nice map here, following out a speedy beginner who always likes to hold the lead. Furthermore, he has good form around a couple of the key chances, and with the likelihood of doing no work and being the opportunist late, he could be very hard to hold out over the concluding stages. ALWAYS BE TECHY (11) was brave last week, doing plenty of work from the backrow draw to sit parked and still giving on the line to finish 2nd. He'll be obliged to do the work again, which could make him a sitting shot, but he's going well. SMOKIN STREPPO (2) comes through that same race and potentially gets a softer map now from the draw. He's been very consistent against similar company, so will go very close with Glen Craven aboard. NORMANDY NUGGET (1) is a quick beginner who likes to lead and was too good from the same draw last week. However, he was beaten fair and square by Smokin Streppo two runs back, which provides a good form reference for this. WINGATE GUY (10) has been given some ace steers lately from Leedham but has just fallen short. He's worth consideration again despite the draw. SELECTIONS:AMERICAN SQUARED (8), ALWAYS BE TECHY (11), SMOKIN STREPPO (2), NORMANDY NUGGET (1)

OVERVIEW:IMAGINATION ORO (2) looks well placed, dropping well back in class and finding a race where she can lead, as she did last time when narrowly beaten by an in-form horse. Her runs earlier this preparation were solid against good company, and the last time she had a similar set-up, she was able to lead and win in good time at Terang. The claim of Hannah Lewis, who's in good form, is a plus over this trip. FIVE CENT (9) gets the trail through from the back row and can be the beneficiary if there's too much tempo early, as he's not afraid to hang tough in his races. He's got a nice record at this track, which also helps. BLACK OPAL JACK (10) is a horse racing better than his form suggests but has another tricky draw to overcome. His strong SP profile speaks to the respect punters have for him, so despite needing luck, he must be kept safe. DARETODANCE (4) and JAMES GARNER (5) are both going well but have slightly tricky draws to overcome here. They're in the mix, while BOBBYS ROOM (1) and A ROCKNROLL JET (8) both have soft draws on the peg line behind the top pick, so while this is harder than they've faced recently, they're worth including in exotics. BACK: IMAGINATION ORO (2) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:IMAGINATION ORO (2), FIVE CENT (9), BLACK OPAL JACK (10), DARETODANCE (4)

OVERVIEW:ARMOURY (3) is a 3yo filly who has impressed in her three starts for new trainer Alex Ashwood, placing on each occasion from bad draws and challenging set-ups. She's finally well drawn and well graded with the mares' allowance and can take a more forward position to prove hard to beat over the short trip. CALYPSO MISTRESS (1) may represent some value in this type of race and gets a positive barrier draw to map well. She can show enough speed to potentially catch the leader's back here, a position she went close to winning from five runs back in similar grade. TRYX VIXEN (4) is a tough filly who likes to race on the pace and was a winner the last time she raced here. Although she may need luck crossing to the pegs, the distance is in her favour. THEROCKGOD (8) will be fitter second up from a break and found the line okay from last seven days ago. He'll be reliant on what unfolds in front of him but looks suited. There are a few others who have claims but will need things to work out, including JOHN WAYNE (7), KEAYANG SANTIAGO (9) and EAGLE MAJOR (10). BACK: ARMOURY (3) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:ARMOURY (3), CALYPSO MISTRESS (1), TRYX VIXEN (4), THEROCKGOD (8)

OVERVIEW:ANAKIN (7) has only placed twice this season, but this looks to be the most suitable race he's been in to return to the winner's circle. He's a horse who races best when put into the race, either in front or outside the leader, so despite the wide draw, he can take the opportunity to control what could be a moderate tempo. Herbertson has partnered him in all four victories. ANIMADO (8) is awkwardly drawn but will appreciate this class, distance and track, where he's recorded more than a third of his career wins. He's been going well up in grade from better draws, but his last win did come when he came with one run from the peg line. JUST MY LUCK (6) has really improved in his past four runs, showing his versatility in those performances. He may float across from this position, look for the right cover and be right in the finish. OUR MYSTERY BET (4) has narrowly missed in his past couple, going down by a head on both occasions. This is a harder assignment, but he's honest and likes this track. MIDNIGHT DIVA (9) was good in winning last start, and although this is slightly harder, keep safe despite the draw. OHHEMMJAY CRESCO (1) can show good speed but is up in class, even though he gets a decent map. BACK: ANAKIN (7) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS:ANAKIN (7), ANIMADO (8), JUST MY LUCK (6), MIDNIGHT DIVA (9)

OVERVIEW:SWEETSUCCESS (5) made an impression earlier in the season, taking on arguably one of the best 2yos in the country in Ideal Frankie and placing behind her on both occasions at her only two starts. She was put out to spell and mature following those terrific performances and has had a solid base of three trials leading into this for a forward showing. MY MATE FLICKA (1) was well supported on debut but did things wrong, costing himself a winning chance, although he still ran well. With that experience, more fitness and a better draw, he can be an improver. ALTO CORAGGIO (10) has burned punters' fingers on a few occasions now, going down as an odds-on favourite, and after seemingly having every hope last start, you'd have to say he was disappointing. The ability is there, so don't dismiss him. DAYSOFWINEN ROSES (7) had only two starts in her preparation earlier this year and has had two trials leading into this. She looked to have some ability last time in, so despite the draw, she's worth consideration. AMANDO (9) was well supported last time but dropped out badly. It's worth noting he's won a trial since, so keep him safe. BACK: SWEETSUCCESS (5) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:SWEETSUCCESS (5), MY MATE FLICKA (1), ALTO CORAGGIO (10), DAYSOFWINEN ROSES (7)

OVERVIEW:AUSSIE JAY MAC (9) is a horse who's far from foolproof, but when he puts things together, he has plenty of talent. Last week at Melton, he punched through from the back row, paced roughly and regained his rhythm before working hard to find the lead and knocking up late. His form prior was very good at this track, and if he races more tractably, he can be hard to hold out. WIND SOCK (8) changes stables to Patrick Tompkinson, who's striking at 18% this season, and Herbertson is also booked. He gets a soft trailing draw off what may be a decent early tempo, so expect him to be strong with clear running. MUSSEL SHOALS (2) failed as favourite last week at Echuca, but her chances hinged on finding the front, which she couldn’t do, and she was forced to work. The map does look more favourable this time for her to bounce back. FLIP A COIN (5) won that race but has a trickier draw to contend with now, although he must be kept safe. SKYFALL BENCHMARK (4) is resuming here off three trials and has a good record at this track. He can map reasonably well from this draw with speed inside and out, and although he'll benefit from the run, he's in the mix. MASTER MIKI (1) needs to lift on recent efforts, but the draw helps his chances of returning to better form. SELECTIONS:AUSSIE JAY MAC (9), WIND SOCK (8), MUSSEL SHOALS (2), MASTER MIKI (1)

OVERVIEW:HELLOVATIME (9) drops sharply back in grade here and has been racing better than his numerical form may suggest. Overall, he's been terrific this season and races well at this track, having only missed a place twice here. The trailing draw is suitable for him to be within striking distance and show his class in the concluding stages. BANDIT EYES (10) comes out of a much stronger race at Melton, where he was sent out as favourite but was poor after finding the lead and was beaten by a big margin. He looks well placed here, being eligible with a claiming price, along with stablemate LILSTREPO (11), who returns to Victoria after a stint in Queensland. She can be competitive despite the draw. WICKED MITZI (8) was back to her best form last week, leading all the way at Echuca, where those tactics are well suited. This draw is a little awkward, and OH SWEET CREATURE (7) also has a tricky map from out wide after racing in better company at Melton. The chances don't end there, with IM DUSTEE (4) and OWEN THE SAINTS (5) having better draws but finding a much stronger race here. SELECTIONS:HELLOVATIME (9), BANDIT EYES (10), LILSTREPO (11), WICKED MITZI (8)

OVERVIEW: The standing-start Kyabram Trotters Cup here over the long 2690m, which really assists the runners off big handicaps. KENNYWOULD (11) has been adept under standing-start conditions recently, winning the St Arnaud Cup from the front-row draw when leading all the way, with a fair margin back to the third horse. He was good prior to that from the tapes again, and you could make a case that this race looks easier than those. Alford partnering him is a plus. JILLIBY TOPGUN (9) is enjoying his best season, trotting much better and developing a good strike rate, winning six from 17 this year. He's first up off one trial, so fitness over the trip may be a query, but his form stands out compared to most of the opposition. ABBIE (10) doesn't have a good record from the stand, with only one placing from 11 attempts, but she's an honest mare who boasts more than double the wins of her nearest rival. She was a good winner three runs back at this track and hasn't had much luck in her past couple in harder grade. They look to be the key winning hopes, with SAINT EYES (7) and LINDY GRACE (8), both last-start winners, appearing the strongest chances for the minor money. BACK: KENNYWOULD (11) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:KENNYWOULD (11), JILLIBY TOPGUN (9), ABBIE (10), SAINT EYES (7)

OVERVIEW:OUR TRUE COLOURS (3) has been well placed in her past couple and is getting closer to cracking it for a win down in grade. The front-row draw suits her to press forward and map well in a race that doesn't have a great deal of depth compared to what she's faced in the past. She's an 11-time winner, while many of these have only recently come out of maiden grade. HALF PRICE BRIDE (8) will appreciate mares' class after racing in stronger company and performing well in her past few, often from bad draws. This one's a little tricky also, but her class is too hard to ignore despite needing luck. WHERES WOOD WOOD (9) is ever-honest, and although she appears to be down on form in her past four runs, she's often had a bit to overcome, so expect her to bounce back to her best against this line-up. QUEENHIGH FLUSH (6) hasn't been having much luck from tricky draws, and while that may be the case again, she's performing better than most. She's in the mix. BETTERTHANABOUGHTONE (7) has claims on her best form, but she hasn't won since January, and the draw hurts. She's still worth a mention. SELECTIONS:OUR TRUE COLOURS (3), HALF PRICE BRIDE (8), WHERES WOOD WOOD (9), QUEENHIGH FLUSH (6)

OVERVIEW:THE PRIVATE DEAL (4) has been most unlucky not to have already won a maiden for the Douglas camp, with the most recent evidence coming last start at Kilmore, where she was climbing all over them before flashing late when clear. She can be a little risky in the score-up, but if she completes that section of the race well, she can remove luck from the equation and prove too strong for these. ARTIES COURAGE (8) presents as the only danger, having bumped into a couple of smart ones in her two career starts. She sat parked last time and was tough, and she's had a tick-over trial since then. She's a little awkwardly drawn here, but there's not much depth to the opposition, so she's right in it. The form of the others doesn't measure up to the top pair, so you're looking at the map to find the minor players. CRESCO THUNDERSTRUCK (1), GLENANGE MISS (2) and ALCATRAZ MISS (3) appear the most likely to get the economical runs needed to feature. BACK: THE PRIVATE DEAL (4) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:THE PRIVATE DEAL (4), ARTIES COURAGE (8), CRESCO THUNDERSTRUCK (1), GLENANGE MISS (2)

OVERVIEW:ARRAPS (9) was going to be in the finish last week at Echuca but raced roughly just as he was making his run around the tighter track, putting paid to his chances and finishing 6th. His form prior was good, particularly at this track, and although his best pattern is when he can lead, he looks well suited on the ratings scale. SALSBOY (7) will most likely map negatively, as he did last start in similar circumstances, but he still found the line quite well. The middle distance may help him work into the fray at the right time. JOEYS HANGOVER (8) has tended to mix his form this season but is also well suited back in class. He'll get a cosy run, so can let down late when the breaks appear. MYNAMEISRUBY (2) is a Herbertson map play by virtue of likely finding the pegs and getting an economical run, but she does need to lift a little all the same. IVE AN IDEA (3) and FAKE CULLECTION (4) may also get nice runs, but the other runners have been putting down more reliable sectionals of late. SELECTIONS:ARRAPS (9), SALSBOY (7), JOEYS HANGOVER (8), MYNAMEISRUBY (2)
